K.CC.A.1.summary: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.

K.CC.A.2.summary: Continue from a supplied number within the familiar sequence.

K.CC.A.3.summary: Write 0–20 and use these numerals for set sizes, including the empty set.

K.CC.B.4.summary: Connect the counting process to how many objects there are.

K.CC.B.4.a.summary: Pair each object once with one number word in sequence.

K.CC.B.4.b.summary: The last word gives the total, invariant under rearrangement or counting order.

K.CC.B.4.c.summary: Each successive number means one more object.

K.CC.B.5.summary: Count up to 20 in a line, rectangle, or circle, up to 10 scattered, and produce a requested set of 1–20.

K.CC.C.6.summary: Compare two collections of up to ten objects each.

K.OA.A.1.summary: Represent joining or separating quantities. Objects, movement, sounds, images, words, drawings, and notation are possible modes.

K.OA.A.2.summary: Solve addition and subtraction stories and calculations within 10.

K.OA.A.3.summary: Split a number at most 10 into two parts in multiple ways. Record each with a drawing or equation.

K.OA.A.4.summary: For each starting number 1–9, find its partner to make ten and record it.

K.NBT.A.1.summary: Build and take apart 11–19 as ten individual ones plus 1–9 more. Record the composition or decomposition.

K.MD.A.1.summary: Describe more than one measurable attribute of an object.

K.MD.A.2.summary: Directly compare two objects on a shared attribute and describe the difference.

K.MD.B.3.summary: Classify by given categories, count each, then order the categories by count. Each category has at most ten objects.

K.G.A.1.summary: Name shapes in the surroundings and describe relative positions.

K.G.A.2.summary: Recognize shapes across changes of orientation and size.

K.G.B.4.summary: Compare plane and solid shapes across sizes and orientations using informal attributes.

K.G.B.5.summary: Model real shapes by building from components and by drawing.

K.G.B.6.summary: Combine simple shapes into a larger one.

1.OA.A.1.summary: Solve additive stories within 20 involving increase, decrease, parts and whole, or comparison, with the unknown in all applicable positions.

1.OA.A.2.summary: Solve stories combining three whole numbers with total at most 20.

1.OA.B.3.summary: Use properties of operations to add or subtract.

1.OA.B.4.summary: Interpret subtraction as finding a missing addend.

1.OA.C.5.summary: Relate counting to addition and subtraction.

1.OA.C.6.summary: Calculate within 20 and attain fluency within 10, using strategies such as making ten, known sums, decomposition, and inverses.

1.OA.D.7.summary: Interpret equality and decide whether additive equations are true.

1.OA.D.8.summary: Find an unknown in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers.

1.NBT.A.1.summary: Count to 120 from any starting number below 120, and read, write, and match numerals to quantities in range.

1.NBT.B.2.summary: Interpret both digits of a two-digit number as tens and ones.

1.NBT.B.2.a.summary: Treat a group of ten ones as one ten.

1.NBT.B.2.b.summary: Recognize 11–19 as one ten plus additional ones.

1.NBT.B.2.c.summary: Interpret 10 through 90 by tens as groups of tens with zero ones.

1.NBT.B.3.summary: Compare two two-digit numbers by tens and ones and record >, = and <.

1.NBT.C.4.summary: Add within 100, including two-digit plus one-digit and two-digit plus a multiple of ten. Use a model or drawing, explain the strategy, and connect it to writing.

1.NBT.C.5.summary: Mentally find ten more or ten less than a two-digit number and explain.

1.NBT.C.6.summary: Subtract multiples of ten, both operands 10–90, with zero or positive difference. Model, explain, and connect to writing.

1.MD.A.1.summary: Order three lengths and use a third object for an indirect comparison.

1.MD.A.2.summary: Measure with repeated equal units placed end to end. Use exact whole-unit spans.

1.MD.B.3.summary: Read and write hours and half-hours on analog and digital clocks.

1.MD.C.4.summary: Organize, display, and interpret up to three categories, including totals, category counts, and differences.

1.G.A.1.summary: Distinguish defining and incidental attributes. Build and draw figures with the defining attributes.

1.G.A.2.summary: Compose plane pieces or solids and use a composite in a further composition.

1.G.A.3.summary: Divide circles and rectangles into two or four equal shares. Name halves, fourths/quarters, reconstruct the whole, and compare share size.

2.OA.A.1.summary: Solve one- and two-step additive stories within 100, across Table 1 situations and unknown positions.

2.OA.B.2.summary: Add and subtract mentally and fluently within 20. By year end recall every sum of two one-digit numbers.

2.OA.C.3.summary: Determine parity for groups up to 20. Express an even count as two equal addends.

2.OA.C.4.summary: Total rectangular arrays up to five rows by five columns using addition. Write the equal-addend equation.

2.NBT.A.1.summary: Interpret three-digit numbers by hundreds, tens, and ones.

2.NBT.A.1.b.summary: Interpret 100 through 900 by hundreds with zero tens and ones.

2.NBT.A.2.summary: Count within 1,000 and skip-count by 5, 10, and 100.

2.NBT.A.3.summary: Read and write numbers to 1,000 as numerals, words, and expanded form.

2.NBT.A.4.summary: Compare three-digit numbers by digit value using >, = and <.

2.NBT.B.5.summary: Fluently add and subtract within 100 using place value, properties, or the inverse relationship.

2.NBT.B.6.summary: Add up to four two-digit numbers using place value and properties.

2.NBT.B.7.summary: Add and subtract within 1,000 with concrete or drawn models linked to writing. Compose or decompose tens and hundreds when needed.

2.NBT.B.8.summary: Mentally add or subtract 10 or 100 from a starting number in 100–900.

2.NBT.B.9.summary: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work using place value and properties of operations. Objects or drawings can support the reasoning.

teaching.reason: Grouping the tickets gives 80 + 20. Opening a hundred and then a ten gives 200 + 90 + 12. Each rearrangement preserves the total.

2.MD.A.1.summary: Select and use an appropriate measuring tool for length.

2.MD.A.2.summary: Measure the same object with two different-size units and relate unit size to the numerical result.

2.MD.A.3.summary: Estimate lengths in inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.

2.MD.A.4.summary: Measure how much longer one object is than another in a standard unit.

2.MD.B.5.summary: Solve same-unit length stories using addition or subtraction within 100.

2.MD.B.6.summary: Show whole numbers as lengths from zero and sums/differences within 100 on an equally spaced number line.

2.MD.C.7.summary: Read and write analog and digital time to five minutes using a.m. and p.m.

2.MD.C.8.summary: Solve money stories with dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies. Use dollar and cent symbols correctly.

2.MD.D.9.summary: Generate length data to the nearest whole unit and make a whole-unit line plot. Repeated measurements of one object are also possible.

2.MD.D.10.summary: Create picture and single-unit bar graphs for up to four categories. Solve simple part/whole and comparison problems using the bar graph.

2.G.A.1.summary: Recognize and draw figures with specified attributes. Identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes.

2.G.A.2.summary: Split a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count them.

2.G.A.3.summary: Divide circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares. Name shares and wholes. Equal shares of identical wholes may have different shapes.

3.OA.A.1.summary: Interpret a whole-number product in context.

3.OA.A.2.summary: Interpret a whole-number quotient both as group size and as number of groups.

3.OA.A.3.summary: Solve multiplication/division problems within 100 involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities.

3.OA.A.4.summary: Find an unknown whole number in a three-quantity multiplication or division equation.

3.OA.B.5.summary: Use operation properties in multiplication and division strategies. Formal property names are optional.

teaching.reason: Both pieces of the split array keep all seven rows. Seven fives and seven threes together make 56.

3.OA.B.6.summary: Interpret division through a missing factor.

3.OA.C.7.summary: Multiply and divide fluently within 100. By year end recall products of every pair of one-digit numbers.

3.OA.D.8.summary: Solve two-step whole-number stories with whole-number answers across the four operations. Use a letter, assess reasonableness mentally or by estimation including rounding, and observe conventional order without parentheses.

3.OA.D.9.summary: Identify arithmetic patterns, including in operation tables, and explain using properties.

3.NBT.A.1.summary: Round whole numbers to the nearest ten or hundred using place value.

3.NBT.A.2.summary: Fluently add and subtract within 1,000 using valid place-value, property, or inverse-based strategies or algorithms.

3.NBT.A.3.summary: Multiply a one-digit whole number by a multiple of ten from 10–90 using place value and properties.

3.NF.A.1.summary: Interpret 1/b as one of b equal parts of a whole and a/b as a such parts.

3.NF.A.2.summary: Represent a fraction as a number on a number line.

3.NF.A.2.a.summary: Partition 0–1 into b equal intervals and locate 1/b at the end of the first.

3.NF.A.2.b.summary: Iterate a lengths of 1/b from zero to locate a/b.

3.NF.A.3.summary: Explain simple equivalence and compare fractions through size.

3.NF.A.3.a.summary: Recognize equal fractions by equal magnitude or coincident number-line points.

3.NF.A.3.b.summary: Recognize, generate, and explain simple equivalent fractions.

3.NF.A.3.c.summary: Express whole numbers as fractions and recognize fractions equal to whole numbers.

3.NF.A.3.d.summary: Compare fractions with common numerator or common denominator using the same whole. Record >, = and < and justify.

3.MD.A.1.summary: Read/write time to the minute, measure intervals in minutes, and solve additive elapsed-time stories.

3.MD.A.2.summary: Measure and estimate mass in g/kg and liquid volume in liters. Solve one-step same-unit stories across the four operations. Exclude compound units, geometric container volume, and multiplicative comparisons.

3.MD.B.3.summary: Draw scaled picture and bar graphs for several categories. Use scaled bars to solve one- and two-step comparison questions.

3.MD.B.4.summary: Measure lengths with rulers marked in halves and fourths of an inch. Plot data on an appropriate whole-, half-, or quarter-unit scale.

3.MD.C.5.summary: Understand area as a measurable property of a plane figure.

3.MD.C.5.a.summary: A square one length unit on each side has area one square unit.

3.MD.C.5.b.summary: A region tiled exactly by n unit squares has area n square units.

3.MD.C.6.summary: Measure by counting unit squares, including square cm, m, in, ft, and improvised square units.

3.MD.C.7.summary: Relate area to multiplication and addition.

3.MD.C.7.a.summary: Tile a whole-number-sided rectangle and show that multiplying its side lengths gives the same area.

3.MD.C.7.b.summary: Use side products in real and mathematical rectangle-area problems, and use rectangular areas to represent whole-number products.

3.MD.C.7.c.summary: Tile a rectangle whose width splits into two parts. Explain the area as the sum of the two products.

teaching.reason: Splitting off one column leaves one square and three more in each row. The two areas add to the original twelve square centimeters.

3.MD.C.7.d.summary: Decompose rectilinear regions into non-overlapping rectangles and add areas, including in applied problems.

3.MD.D.8.summary: Solve polygon-perimeter problems, including a missing side. Exhibit rectangles with equal perimeter/different area and equal area/different perimeter.

3.G.A.1.summary: Classify by shared attributes. Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as quadrilaterals and draw a quadrilateral outside those subcategories.

3.G.A.2.summary: Partition shapes into equal-area parts and express each part as a unit fraction of the whole area.

4.OA.A.1.summary: Read a product equation as a multiplicative comparison and translate a spoken comparison into an equation.

4.OA.A.2.summary: Solve multiplication/division comparison stories and distinguish multiplicative from additive comparison.

4.OA.A.3.summary: Solve multistep whole-number stories with whole-number answers across the four operations. Interpret remainders, represent the unknown by a letter, and assess reasonableness mentally or through estimates including rounding.

4.OA.B.4.summary: For 1–100, find every positive factor pair, relate a number to its factors as a multiple, test for a given one-digit factor, and classify prime/composite where applicable.

4.OA.C.5.summary: Generate a number or shape pattern from a rule, identify features the rule does not state, and explain their persistence informally.

4.NBT.A.1.summary: A digit has ten times the value it has one position to the right.

4.NBT.A.2.summary: Read/write base-ten numerals, words, and expanded forms and compare using >, = and <.

4.NBT.A.3.summary: Round multi-digit whole numbers to any place using place value. The Grade 4 domain extends through one million.

4.NBT.B.4.summary: Fluently add and subtract multidigit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

4.NBT.B.5.summary: Multiply up to four digits by one digit, and two digits by two digits. Use place value and operation properties. Illustrate and explain using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

teaching.reason: Pairing each width with both heights gives four partial products. Their areas add to 322 square units.

4.NBT.B.6.summary: Find whole-number quotients and remainders for up to four-digit dividends and one-digit nonzero divisors. Explain using place value, properties and/or the inverse relationship, with equations, arrays, and/or area models.

4.NF.A.1.summary: Use a visual fraction model to explain generating equivalence by multiplying numerator and denominator by the same positive whole number.

4.NF.A.2.summary: Compare fractions with different numerators and denominators for the same whole. Record >, = and < and justify.

4.NF.B.3.summary: Understand a/b, for a>1, as a sum of a unit fractions.

4.NF.B.3.a.summary: Interpret fraction addition/subtraction as joining/separating amounts that refer to the same whole.

4.NF.B.3.b.summary: Decompose a fraction in more than one way with a common denominator, record equations, and justify.

4.NF.B.3.c.summary: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators.

4.NF.B.3.d.summary: Solve like-denominator fraction addition/subtraction stories with a common whole.

4.NF.B.4.summary: Extend multiplication to a fraction times a whole number.

4.NF.B.4.a.summary: Interpret a/b as a copies of 1/b.

4.NF.B.4.b.summary: Use copies of a unit fraction to calculate a whole-number multiple of a fraction.

4.NF.B.4.c.summary: Solve stories multiplying a fraction by a whole number.

4.NF.C.5.summary: Rename tenths as hundredths and add a tenths fraction to a hundredths fraction.

4.NF.C.6.summary: Write fractions with denominator 10 or 100 in decimal notation.

4.NF.C.7.summary: Compare decimals through hundredths for the same whole. Record >, = and < and justify.

4.MD.A.1.summary: Use relative unit sizes within one system to express larger units in smaller ones. Organize equivalent measurements in a two-column table.

4.MD.A.2.summary: Use four operations in problems about distance, time intervals, liquid volume, mass, and money. Include simple fractions/decimals and conversions from larger units to smaller. Represent quantities with diagrams featuring a measurement scale.

4.MD.A.3.summary: Apply rectangle area and perimeter formulas in applied and mathematical problems.

4.MD.B.4.summary: Display measurement data in halves, quarters, and eighths on line plots. Use the displayed data for fraction sums/differences.

4.MD.C.5.summary: Recognize an angle from two rays sharing an endpoint and understand angle measure.

4.MD.C.5.a.summary: Relate angle to a fraction of a circle centered at the vertex. One degree is 1/360 of a full turn.

4.MD.C.5.b.summary: A turn spanning n one-degree units measures n degrees.

4.MD.C.6.summary: Measure angles to whole-number degrees with a protractor and sketch angles of specified measure.

4.MD.C.7.summary: Use additivity of adjacent, non-overlapping angle parts to find unknowns in diagrams and applied problems.

4.G.A.1.summary: Draw and identify points, lines, segments, rays, right/acute/obtuse angles, and parallel/perpendicular lines in plane figures.

4.G.A.2.summary: Classify plane figures by presence or absence of stated line relationships or angle sizes. Identify right triangles.

4.G.A.3.summary: Identify reflection symmetry, recognize figures having it, and draw lines of symmetry.

5.NBT.B.5.summary: Multiply multidigit whole numbers fluently with the standard algorithm.
